localContext: North Merrick's mix of single-family homes, tree-lined streets, and proximity to parks and green spaces creates ideal conditions for wasp and hornet colonies to establish nests in attics, wall voids, eaves, and soffits. From properties near North Merrick Community Park to homes along Merrick Avenue and the surrounding residential neighborhoods, our team knows the local architecture and common nesting sites that attract wasps, hornets, and yellow jackets in this Nassau County community. Carpenter bees bore into fascia boards, porch beams, and deck railings, while ground-nesting yellow jackets and bumble bees burrow into lawns and landscaping beds.

faqs.question: Do you treat honeybees in North Merrick?
faqs.answer: No, we do not treat honeybees. If an inspection confirms a colony is honeybees rather than wasps or hornets, we refer the situation to a licensed beekeeper instead of treating it ourselves.

faqs.question: How do I know if I have a wasp or hornet nest in my North Merrick home?
faqs.answer: Common signs include seeing large numbers of wasps or hornets entering and exiting a specific area of your home — especially eaves, vents, siding gaps, or soffit seams — hearing buzzing sounds within walls or ceilings, noticing paper nest material visible at an entry point, or finding dead insects inside your home. If you observe consistent stinging-insect activity in one location, especially during spring and summer months, you likely have an established nest that requires professional treatment and removal.
